name: ValueTransform
purpose: Strongly-typed parse/validate step that converts a raw inbound argument (body/query/param) into the typed value the handler expects.
api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, TypeVar
from dataclasses import dataclass

I = TypeVar('I')
O = TypeVar('O')

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ArgumentMetadata:
    kind: str
    metatype: type | None
    data: str | None

class ValueTransform(Protocol):
    def transform(self, value: I, meta: ArgumentMetadata) -> O: ...
invariants: transform() MUST raise a typed validation error on bad input; it NEVER returns None to signal invalid.
A ValueTransform MUST be pure: same (value, meta) SHALL produce the same output with no observable side effects.
metatype MUST drive the coercion target; CANNOT silently ignore the declared type.
Composed transforms MUST apply left-to-right in declaration order; swapping order SHALL be explicit.
NEVER mutates the incoming value in place; the returned value is always fresh.
extension_contract: Downstream tools implement ValueTransform (e.g. a ZodValidationPipe-style class) and bind it with a decorator/register call on a parameter or handler; built-in transforms (ParseInt, Validation) MUST satisfy the same Protocol and compose cleanly.

sources.locator: docs.nestjs.com/pipes — transform(value, metadata: ArgumentMetadata) where kind ∈ body|query|param|custom

sources.source: ASP.NET Core 8.0 — Model binding and validation

why_essential: A handler that receives raw strings has to re-validate the same fields on every path; one contract lets validators/coercers be shared across all entry points and keeps error shapes consistent.
alternatives_considered: Validation inside each handler — duplicated logic, inconsistent errors
Manual parsing with framework helpers only — no composition of custom rules
JSON-Schema only — cannot express cross-field rules cleanly
